speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing difficulties conceiving and discomfort during sexual activity; to help you, I need to know your age and how long you have been trying to conceive. Can you also describe the specific nature of the pain you feel during intercourse?

speaker: Patient
text: 30-year-old female. The patient and her husband have been trying to conceive for 15 months without success. They are sexually active at least twice a week. The husband occasionally has difficulties maintaining an erection. The patient reports discomfort and pelvic floor muscle tension during attempted vaginal penetration. Diagnosed with body dysmorphic disorder three years ago. No family history of serious illness. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. No medications.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Dyspareunia (likely vestibulodynia or pelvic floor myofascial pain syndrome) secondary to body dysmorphic disorder.

Thank you for the detailed history. While your age and duration of infertility (15 months) meet the criteria for clinical investigation, your report of pelvic floor tension and pain on penetration strongly suggests a gynecological or psychological cause. Given your diagnosis of body dysmorphic disorder, we should consider how this impacts your pelvic floor muscles and sexual function. Have you noticed any specific physical triggers for the pain, such as certain positions or touch, or is it constant? Also, has your husband undergone any evaluation for his erectile difficulties?
